verifications.note: Anadarko's July 20, 2007 press release: the Independence Trail pipeline 'connects with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at Enterprise's West Delta block 68 shallow-water manifold platform. The pipeline is approximately 134 miles long, 24 inches in diameter and has the capacity to transport up to 1 Bcf/d' -- 1 Bcf/d = 1,000 MMcf/d, an exact match.

Genesis Energy, L.P. FY2018 Form 10-K, offshore natural gas pipelines table: 'Independence Trail | Genesis | 135 | 1,000 | 100%' (System Miles | Design Capacity MMcf/day | Interest Owned) -- exact match on capacity.

Genesis's July 16, 2015 Form 8-K Exhibit 99.3 (historical financials of the acquired Enterprise Offshore Business): pipeline table lists 'Independence Trail ... 100.0% ... 135 [miles] ... 1,000' Approximate Net Capacity (MMcf/d) -- exact match, pre-dating the Genesis acquisition.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Capacity=1000.00 MMcf/d is confirmed by three independent sources spanning three eras of the pipeline's ownership: Anadarko's 2007 in-service press release ('up to 1 Bcf/d'), Enterprise's own pre-divestiture historical financials filed as Genesis's July 2015 8-K Exhibit 99.3 ('1,000' MMcf/d Approximate Net Capacity), and Genesis's FY2018 10-K pipeline-systems table ('1,000' MMcf/day Design Capacity). All three name the Independence Trail pipeline specifically and agree exactly.

verifications.note: OGJ, Jan. 12, 2006: 'The Independence Trail pipeline, wholly owned by an Enterprise affiliate, is a new 134-mile, 24-in. pipeline that will transport production from the platform to an interconnection with Tennessee Gas Pipeline on West Delta Block 68.' Exact match on diameter.
Anadarko's July 2007 press release: '...approximately 134 miles long, 24 inches in diameter...' Exact match.

Jahde (2007), TMS conference paper on the pipeline's engineering design: required Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure 'necessitates an outside pipeline diameter of 24 inches Double Submerged Arc Welded (DSAW)...' Exact match.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Diameter=24 in is confirmed exactly and independently by trade press (OGJ 2006), the operator/co-owner's own 2007 press release (Anadarko), and a peer-reviewed engineering paper specific to this pipeline's construction (Jahde 2007). No conflicting diameter figure found anywhere.

Genesis's 10-K lists Independence Trail under the heading 'Offshore natural gas pipelines' and states it 'transports natural gas from certain pipeline interconnects to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline.'

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Fuel=Gas is trivially and unanimously confirmed -- every source describes Independence Trail as a natural-gas transportation pipeline; no source describes it carrying any other product.

verifications.note: Genesis FY2018 10-K: 'The Independence Trail pipeline transports natural gas from certain pipeline interconnects to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at a pipeline interconnect on the West Delta 68 pipeline junction platform. Natural gas transported on the Independence Trail Pipeline can originate from production fields in the Atwater Valley, DeSoto Canyon, Lloyd Ridge and Mississippi Canyon areas of the Gulf of Mexico.'

Genesis's 2015 8-K Ex. 99.3 (Enterprise Offshore Business historicals): 'The Independence Trail pipeline transports natural gas from the Independence Hub platform and a pipeline interconnect downstream of the Independence Hub platform to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at a pipeline interconnect on the West Delta 68 pipeline junction platform. Natural gas transported on the Independence Trail pipeline originates from production fields in the Atwater Valley, DeSoto Canyon, Lloyd Ridge and Mississippi Canyon areas of the Gulf of Mexico.'

resolutions.researcher_notes: LIKELY CONTRADICTS THE SHEET AS A SCHEMA/DEFINITION MISMATCH. Recorded FuelSource='West Delta Block 68' is not supported in the sense of an originating gas field -- two independent, pipeline-naming SEC filings (Genesis's 2015 8-K Ex.99.3 and FY2018 10-K, filed four years apart) both explicitly and identically describe West Delta 68 as the pipeline's DOWNSTREAM delivery interconnect with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline, and separately state the gas actually ORIGINATES from production fields in the Atwater Valley, DeSoto Canyon, Lloyd Ridge and Mississippi Canyon areas (i.e., via the Independence Hub platform at Mississippi Canyon Block 920, and other interconnects upstream of West Delta 68). No source anywhere describes West Delta 68 itself as a producing field. Recommend FuelSource describe the origin fields/Independence Hub rather than West Delta Block 68 (which is really the Location/interconnect value) -- flagging for Update routing per this pass's brief; not applying the value change here, only sourcing what the refs state.

verifications.note: Jahde (2007): 'At a record water depth of 7,912 fsw in the Gulf of Mexico, the 138 mile long Independence [Trail Pipeline]...' Exact match to recorded 138.00 mi.
Anadarko's 2007 press release: pipeline is 'approximately 134 miles long.' Close to, but 4 mi (~3%) short of, the recorded 138 mi.
Genesis FY2018 10-K pipeline table: Independence Trail listed at '135' System Miles. 3 mi short of the recorded 138 mi.

offshore-technology.com: 'Enterprise also installed 140 miles (225km) of 24in-diameter pipeline ... Owned and operated by Enterprise, the pipeline is called Independence Trail.' 2 mi longer than the recorded 138 mi.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Length=138.00 mi is matched EXACTLY by one strong primary source: Jahde (2007), a peer-reviewed engineering conference paper written by a pipeline-construction engineer specifically about Independence Trail's design and installation ('the 138 mile long Independence [Trail]...'). However, every other source found gives a somewhat different figure for the same pipeline: OGJ's Nov. 2006 special report says 'a high-pressure, 132-mile pipeline'; OGJ's Jan. 2006 article and Anadarko's July 2007 press release both say 134 miles; Genesis's own FY2018 10-K regulatory table says 135 System Miles; offshore-technology.com's project page says 140 miles. That is a genuine 132-140 mile spread (~6%) across six independent, pipeline-naming sources, with only the specialist engineering paper landing on the sheet's exact 138 mi -- flagging this as a material validity/spec concern (per the contract's rounding-discrepancy rule) rather than treating 138 mi as uncontested. Classing REFS_ADDED (an exact-match source was found) rather than UNRESOLVED, but tier/independent are set conservatively given the spread; recommend a closer look at which figure (design vs. as-built vs. a route revision over the project's multi-year construction, 2003-2007) best matches GEM's LengthKnown convention.

verifications.note: Anadarko: the pipeline 'connects with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at Enterprise's West Delta block 68 shallow-water manifold platform,' running from the Independence Hub platform which is sited on 'Mississippi Canyon Block 920.' Confirms both recorded endpoint names.

offshore-technology.com: 'The pipeline redelivered the production from Independence Hub into the Tennessee Gas Pipeline, located in West Delta 68'; separately states the Independence Hub platform's 'Location Mississippi Canyon Block 920.' Confirms both endpoint names.

Genesis 10-K: 'The Independence Trail pipeline transports natural gas ... to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at a pipeline interconnect on the West Delta 68 pipeline junction platform.' Confirms West Delta 68 as the named endpoint.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both recorded location values are confirmed by multiple independent sources: the pipeline runs between the Independence Hub platform at Mississippi Canyon Block 920 (recorded EndLocation) and an interconnect with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at the West Delta 68 pipeline junction platform (recorded StartLocation). Note for validity, not a value error: every source describes the physical gas flow as originating at Mississippi Canyon 920 (the Hub) and terminating at West Delta 68 (the delivery interconnect) -- i.e., flow runs End-to-Start relative to GEM's Start/End labels on this row. Since GEM's Start/End convention does not necessarily track physical flow direction, this is flagged as a spec/validity note only, not a proposed change to the two location names themselves, which are both independently confirmed as correct.

resolutions.researcher_notes: CONTRADICTS THE SHEET (ownership is stale). Recorded Owner1=Enterprise Products Partners 100.00% is supported by period sources only through the pipeline's original construction/early-operating years (OGJ 2006: 'wholly owned by an Enterprise affiliate'; Anadarko's 2007 press release similarly frames Enterprise as the pipeline owner/counterparty). But Genesis Energy, L.P.'s July 16, 2015 Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.3, discloses Genesis's acquisition of Enterprise's Gulf of Mexico 'Offshore Business' -- explicitly naming 'Independence Trail' by name in the acquired asset table at 100% ownership interest -- and Genesis's own FY2018 10-K (filed 2019-02-28, more than three years later) lists 'Independence Trail' in its offshore natural gas pipeline systems table with Operator/Owner = 'Genesis' at 100% interest. No source found after July 2015 attributes ownership to Enterprise Products Partners. Recommend Owner1=Genesis Energy, L.P. 100.00% (effective ~July 2015) in place of the currently recorded Enterprise Products Partners -- flagging for Update/ownership-sweep routing per this pass's brief; not applying the value change here, only sourcing what the refs actually state.

verifications.note: OGJ, Nov. 27, 2006: the operators 'proposed to build the platform and pipeline in 2003, with procurement starting in 2004 along with the agreements for the ownership infrastructure, processing, and transportation.'

resolutions.researcher_notes: Only one source found that assigns specific calendar years to the project's proposal/commitment stage: OGJ's Nov. 2006 special report states the Independence Hub platform AND pipeline were 'proposed to build ... in 2003, with procurement starting in 2004.' The recorded ProposalYear=2004 matches the procurement-start year given here (a 1-year discrepancy from the 2003 proposal date in the same sentence) -- treated as within-rounding agreement per the contract's discrepancy rule rather than a contradiction, since both years come from the same primary account of one continuous commitment process. Single source only (no second, independent source found that names a specific proposal year), so tier is medium and independent=false rather than high.

Could NOT confirm 'operating' as the CURRENT status, and found signals pointing the other way, but nothing specific enough naming Independence Trail to propose a replacement value. Genesis Energy's FY2018 10-K (filed 2019-02-28) still lists 'Independence Trail' in its offshore natural-gas-pipeline systems table with a live capacity/length/ownership entry, supporting 'operating' as of fiscal year-end 2018. But Genesis's FY2019 10-K (filed 2020-02-27) drops Independence Trail from that same table entirely -- the table jumps directly from the header to 'High Island Offshore System' with no Independence Trail line -- and the ONLY 'Independence' occurrence anywhere in that 10-K is the unrelated phrase 'Director Independence' in the table of contents. Separately, offshore-technology.com's project page states production from the associated Independence Hub platform 'was stopped in December 2015 and decommissioning was completed in 2019,' and Genesis's Q4-2023 earnings 8-K (filed 2024-02-15) states 'On April 29, 2022, we sold our Independence Hub platform and recognized a gain on the sale of $40.0 million.' None of these documents makes an explicit, dated statement that the Independence Trail PIPELINE itself (as opposed to the Hub platform, a related but distinct asset) stopped operating, was idled, or was decommissioned -- so I am not proposing a specific replacement status (shelved/idle/decommissioned) without a source that names the pipeline directly. Also searched: PHMSA's National Pipeline Mapping System / incident database and general web search for 'Independence Trail pipeline decommissioned OR abandoned OR idle' -- nothing found naming the pipeline (not the Hub) with a specific out-of-service date. Flagging the FY2018-to-FY2019 disappearance from Genesis's own asset table, read together with the Hub's 2015 production-stop/2019-decommissioning and 2022 platform sale, as a strong status-review candidate for the orchestrator to route -- but classing UNRESOLVED rather than asserting a specific new status I cannot source.
